mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during inflation spikes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not exceed 0.3% in at least 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor compensation growth of at least 0.5% signals wage stickiness and corporate hiring momentum, which elevates expected future profits and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth rate ≥ 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes meeting the trigger, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or monthly PAYEMS growth < 0.5% for 6 consecutive months after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index (≥ 2.0% month-over-month decline) indicates weakening industrial demand, which compresses forward discounting and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During INDPRO contraction periods, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or INDPRO recovers by ≥ 1.5% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both HOUST retail sales and RSAFS financial sector demand (each ≥ 1.5% month-over-month) creates a dual-demand surge that amplifies equity risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST ↑ ≥ 1.5% AND RSAFS ↑ ≥ 1.5% in the same month
failure_condition: During qualifying months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or either HOUST or RSAFS growth < 1.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.50% for two consecutive months, the anticipation of higher borrowing costs suppresses equity valuation growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.50% and remains ≥ 4.50% in the following month
failure_condition: During high-rate periods, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4.50% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE unemployment (≤ 3.0% for two consecutive months) in a post-recession context is interpreted as labor market tightening, which elevates risk premia and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly rate falls to ≤ 3.0% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market tightening after weak recovery
failure_condition: During tightening periods, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or UNRATE > 3.0% in the subsequent month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditures (≥ 2.0% decline) suggests consumption weakness, which reduces expected growth in corporate earnings and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During such episodes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or GDPC1 recovers by ≥ 1.0% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.50% for three consecutive months in a low-rate environment, the expectation of future easing supports risk-on sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During low-rate holds, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rises above 1.50% in any of the three months.
